faq: Should I ask for a card at the start?
Both work. A no-card trial often brings in more sign-ups, while a card trial often converts a higher share to paid. We explain each, and you choose. We do not promise results.
What happens to a customer's data when a trial ends?
We keep it, and the account moves to a limited or read-only state, based on your choice. If they upgrade later, everything is still there.
Can you stop people from starting repeat trials?
We can add sensible checks, such as one trial per email and per company. Nobody can block every repeat sign-up, but these checks reduce it without annoying genuine users.
Do I need a payment provider set up already?
For a card trial, yes, such as Stripe. For a no-card trial it is not required at first. If you need to set one up, our payment provider setup service covers it.
desc:
Free trial setup for SaaS subscriptions, delivered by Ecom Swift LLC. We build a trial that starts at sign-up, counts the days, sends reminders and moves the customer onto a paid plan, with a limited state instead of a deleted account at the end.

## What is a free trial in a subscription product?

A free trial is a fixed period in which a new user can use your product before paying. There are two common designs. In a card-on-file trial, the customer enters payment details at the start and is charged automatically when the trial ends unless they cancel. In a no-card trial, the customer signs up with only an email address and decides later whether to subscribe.

Both designs need a clear start date, an end date, a visible countdown and a defined outcome. The outcome is the part people forget: what the account looks like when the days run out and no payment has been made.

## Why the trial design shapes who becomes a paying customer

A trial exists to let a person reach the moment where the product proves its value. If the trial is too short, people leave before they see it. If it has no reminders, they forget it exists. If it ends with a locked screen and no explanation, a person who might have paid walks away annoyed.

The card choice changes the audience. Asking for a card at the start usually attracts fewer sign-ups with higher intent, while skipping the card lets more people try the product and puts more weight on your reminders and upgrade prompts. Neither is always better, and the right answer depends on your price, your product and how fast a new user sees value. We help you choose and build the one you pick.

## What a good trial includes

- One trial length per plan, chosen to match how long it takes to see the product's value.
- Trial start and end dates saved on the customer account.
- A visible days-left indicator inside the app.
- A choice between card-on-file and no-card sign-up.
- Reminder emails shortly before the trial ends, and one on the final day.
- An upgrade button that is always in reach, not hidden in settings.
- An automatic first charge when a card was collected, with a receipt.
- A limited-access state when the trial ends without payment, with data kept safe.
- Protection against repeat trials from the same person, where practical.
- A simple view of how many trials turned into paid plans.

## How we build it

We start by agreeing the rules with you: trial length, card or no card, what a customer can do during the trial and what happens afterwards. Then we connect the trial to your billing provider, so the clock and the first charge follow the same dates. The Basic package covers one trial length, saved dates, a days-left display and limited access after the end. The Standard package adds the card or no-card choice, reminder emails, an upgrade button and the automatic first charge, with a test run through the whole trial. The Premium package adds different trial lengths per plan, a one-time extension, a trial-ending banner and email set, a trial to paid report and a handover call.

We test by moving test accounts through every date, including the day before the end, the day after and a cancellation in the middle. Ecom Swift LLC cannot promise a conversion rate, because that depends on your product and audience.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Tell people on the sign-up page exactly when the trial ends and what happens then.
- Remind customers before the end, not only after it.
- Keep customer data safe when the trial lapses.
- Make upgrading a single click from any screen.
- Decide in advance how support may grant an extension.

**Avoid:**
- Charging a card without a clear warning email first.
- Deleting accounts the moment a trial ends.
- Hiding the end date or the cancel option.
- Allowing unlimited repeat trials with the same email address.
- Setting a trial so short that nobody reaches the useful part of the product.

## Who this is for

This service suits a new SaaS product launching its first paid plans. It suits a team that currently offers free access with no clear path to payment. It also suits a business whose trial emails are written by hand each time and want the whole process automated.

## What we need from you

Tell us how long the trial should last, whether you want a card at sign-up and what a trial user may and may not do. You do not need a finished payment provider setup to begin, but you will need one before the card-on-file option can run. Give us developer or collaborator access to your app and a team role in your provider account. We never need passwords. After ordering, we send a short checklist and a test account for you to try.
